text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Streaming p99 latency spike on /v1/stream/sse (eu-west-1). p99 ~4.2s, baseline ~0.6s. Affected ~7% of streaming requests. Paging on-call now.
kevin: ack — I'm oncall, starting triage.
kevin: joining call in 2m, posting initial checklist: check proxy pools, recent deploys, client backpressure metrics.
ops-bot: paging teams: @eng-runtime @eng-sre @support.
maya: seeing queue depth climb on proxy-02 (eu-west-1). netstat shows a bunch of SYN_RECV -> ESTABLISHED with long write queues.
lina: grabbing logs from proxy-02 now. tail -n 200 /var/log/proxy/proxy.log | grep -i "chunk" | tail -n 80
lina: ```
2026-03-17T02:13:45Z proxy-02 write timeout after 30000ms for conn id=0x7f8a
2026-03-17T02:13:46Z proxy-02 client stalled: window=0, buffered_bytes=1.2MB
2026-03-17T02:13:47Z proxy-02 upstream write backlog 512 KB
```
kevin: logs look like client-side backpressure (window=0) causing proxy buffers to grow and increasing tail latency. p95 also creeping up.
maya: correlated with router rollout at ~02:14 UTC — router v1.3.8 canary went to 25% then paused. routing layer started different connection reuse pattern.
ryan: did any downstream customer SDKs change? any large clients pushing slow consumers?
lina: checking client metrics — saw a single heavy customer with many concurrent SSEs and slow reads starting 02:12 UTC.
kevin: mitigation plan (immediate):
  1) enable proxy backpressure circuit for proxy-02 (throttle incoming stream creation)
  2) increase upstream keepalive to reduce timeouts while we drain
  3) reroute traffic off proxy-02 to proxy-04 (eu-west-1) for 10m rolling drain
  4) notify CS and update status page draft
kevin: ops-bot, run: `/proxy toggle-backpressure --host proxy-02 --enable --threshold 512KB`
ops-bot: executing `/proxy toggle-backpressure --host proxy-02 --enable --threshold 512KB` ... 
ops-bot: done — backpressure enabled on proxy-02 (threshold=524288).
kevin: starting drain of proxy-02: `/scripts/drain-proxy proxy-02 --grace 60s`
ops-bot: drain started, shifting traffic away (expected <5% request failures during drain).
cs-erin: drafting status: "We are investigating increased streaming latency in EU region; some streaming connections may see delays up to 10s. Mitigation in progress." Will post if we have a stable update.
lina: after enabling backpressure, seeing immediate drop in buffered bytes on proxy-02. p99 -> 1.1s, p95 -> 0.45s (pre-mitigation p99=4.2s).
maya: adding temporary route rule to limit long-lived SSE connections per IP for 30m.
ryan: great — also recommend we pause router canary until we confirm stability.
kevin: paused router rollout at 25%.
kevin: runbook checks: check KV cache sizes, because long lived streams were growing per-connection caches; schedule TTL enforcement for cached prefixes if needed.
lina: capturing diagnostic bundle and uploading to paste: https://paste.internal/abc123 (logs + metrics snapshot).
cs-erin: notifying top impacted customer contact list; will offer workaround: reconnect or switch to polling endpoint if critical.
kevin: monitoring for 10m. If p99 stays <1.5s and client buffering resolves, we'll consider incident mitigated and start RCA.
maya: monitoring dashboards show stabilization at 02:20 UTC, no new spike after drain.
ryan: who owns RCA? need owner for follow-up (deploy cause vs. client behavior).
kevin: I'll own the RCA. tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre.
cs-erin: we'll wait for final confirmation before sending an incident summary to customers.
kevin: quick note for postmortem: plausible cause = interaction between router connection reuse behavior + a heavy slow-consumer client causing proxy buffer growth -> tail latency. Mitigations that worked: enable backpressure circuit, drain offending host, pause router rollout, limit long-lived SSE per IP.
ops-bot: incident state: mitigated (p99 back to 1.1s). Will reopen if metrics regress.
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: p99 stabilized. Follow-up: RCA doc + action items assigned.
kevin: Thanks all — adding action items: (1) add automatic detection for slow-consumer-induced buffer growth, (2) add a safety limit to router connection reuse pattern, (3) add guidance to CS for customer workaround.
cs-erin: will prepare customer-facing note once RCA has final language.
kevin: closing the on-call thread, monitoring for 30m. :thumbsup:
